subject: Urgent: contract spend-cap enforcement & graceful fallback for Vertex
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora@vertexfinance.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: VF-238: must-have: monthly spend ceiling + graceful fallback

Hi Marissa and Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Vertex is excited about Redwood for our customer-facing assistants. Before we move to signature, Legal has pushed back on a specific operational requirement we need in the SOW and was asked to surface it here so we can get engineering guidance on feasibility and timelines.

TL;DR: We need a contractually enforced monthly spend ceiling per account (hard cap) that can be configured per-deal. When the cap is reached, calls should be throttled with a well-defined graceful failure mode (fallback response or 429/503) and an automatic invoice credit line for excess usage beyond the cap during the billing month.

Key details from Legal/Finance:
- Per-customer monthly token ceiling (numeric value in tokens) that we set at activation.
- Behavior options when cap hits: (A) reject with 429 and no inference, (B) reject but return cached/summarized answer, or (C) route to a lower-cost summary model with deterministic token bounds.
- Auto-credit calculation for any overage within the billing month (they want an automated adjustment, not just a manual credit).
- Audit evidence: logs showing when caps were hit and what fallback was executed.

Attachments: SOW_draft_v2.pdf (redlined), usage_report_Q2.csv (sample consumption).

Is this something you can scope? We need to know whether this is: (1) doable with a small engineering change in a few weeks, (2) requires a multi-sprint product project, or (3) needs a contractual workaround.

Appreciate a quick reality-check.

— Nora
Nora Patel
VP, Platform Engineering | Vertex Finance

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora@vertexfinance.com>, Vertex Legal <contracts@vertexfinance.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VF-238: must-have: monthly spend ceiling + graceful fallback

Connor / Priyom — looping you both in to triage. This is a critical close condition for VF-238 (they indicated this is required to sign). Deal team has committed to go-live in 6 weeks from signature; finance needs the automated credit behavior to avoid manual reconciliation.

Questions for Product/Eng:
- Can we support a per-account token cap enforced at the gateway level with a configurable fallback option?
- What are the minimal audit logs we can provide to satisfy Legal?
- Estimate: MVP timeline and a fast workaround if full automation isn't feasible immediately.

I can push for a short-term clause in the SOW if we can promise to deliver a workaround within 3 weeks.

Thanks,
— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VF-238: must-have: monthly spend ceiling + graceful fallback

Hi — quick technical read. High level: this is doable but the implementation surface has non-trivial product and billing implications. I sketched three options below (tradeoffs and rough timelines).

Option 1 — Enforcement at ingress (Gateway Hard Cap)
- Behavior: gateway tracks per-account tokens in real time and rejects requests after cap.
- Pros: deterministic enforcement, simple from Legal's perspective.
- Cons: requires stateful counters per account, cross-region sync if they use multiple regions, ~6–8 week effort (infra + billing hooks + audit logs).

Option 2 — Soft cap + automated crediting (Fast path)
- Behavior: allow requests to continue, emit alerts when cap hit, then run an automated billing job at month-end to apply credits. Could also implement request-level soft-fail (429) via feature flag.
- Pros: much faster (2–3 weeks) because most work is billing automation and QoS flags.
- Cons: not a true hard prevention; Legal may push back unless we add strong SLAs for the credit workflow.

Option 3 — Fallback routing to summary model (Hybrid)
- Behavior: upon cap, route to a bounded, low-cost summarization model (token-limited) or cached response.
- Pros: preserves UX, lower cost; can be feature-flagged per-account.
- Cons: needs model routing and deterministic token bounds; ~4–6 weeks.

Audit/logging: we can surface events (cap_check, cap_hit, fallback_executed) in Console and export JSON audit logs. For full legal-grade evidence, we'll need retention policy alignment and a signed SLA for log retention.

Immediate asks from me:
1) Product decision: do we require a hard cap at launch or is VF ok with a soft cap + automated credits (Option 2) as a stopgap?
2) If hard cap required, prioritize ticketing for stateful counters and billing integration.

I'll spare the infra design until we pick an option.

— Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior SWE, Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora@vertexfinance.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VF-238: must-have: monthly spend ceiling + graceful fallback

Thanks — my product perspective below. I spoke with Billing and Platform infra. Key constraints and a proposed path: 

Constraints:
- Billing: our invoicing system expects post-hoc adjustments; real-time credits are possible but require a clear trigger and audit trail.
- Runtime: per-account counters with global consistency are heavier work, but per-region caps are acceptable if documented.

Proposed path (reduce risk, hit-close timeline):
Week 0–1 (fast workaround):
- Deploy feature-flagged soft-cap at gateway that responds with a friendly 409/429 and a header X-Redwood-Cap-Status when a soft threshold is crossed.
- Enable audit events and a daily job that emits cap-hit summaries to Billing.

Week 2–3 (automated crediting):
- Add a billing automation job that calculates overage & posts credit lines automatically at month close; legal can accept this as automated crediting as long as events are auditable.

Week 4–6 (if hard cap required):
- Build stateful counters and consistent enforcement; ensure cross-region replication or document per-region behavior.

Deliverables for VF to sign:
- An SOW appendix describing soft-cap behavior + timeline to hard cap if needed.
- Console audit export (cap_hit.csv) + sample webhook for real-time notifications.

Recommendation: ship the soft-cap + automated billing credits as the MVP (3 weeks). If Vertex requires a hard block in contract, we scope the hard-cap work as an add-on (4–6 weeks) and include per-region behavior in the SOW.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Product Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora@vertexfinance.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VF-238: must-have: monthly spend ceiling + graceful fallback

Nora — thanks for surfacing this. Based on engineering and product input above, here's what we propose for the SOW appendix and what we'll deliver as part of the VF-238 activation: 

1) MVP (target: 3 weeks from signature) — soft-cap + automated credits
- Soft-cap enforced via gateway feature flag (returns 429 with X-Redwood-Cap-Status header).
- Daily cap-hit export to Billing + automated month-close credit posting.
- Audit CSV export (cap_hit.csv) and sample webhook for events.

2) Optional Add-on (4–6 weeks) — hard cap enforcement
- Stateful per-account counters with rejection at gateway; cross-region behavior documented in SOW.

Legal next steps: if Vertex Legal is comfortable with the automated credit flow described above, we can include the MVP language in the SOW and commit to the add-on timeline for hard enforcement. Otherwise, we will need to scope the hard-cap work into the SOW as a deliverable before signature.

Please confirm which path you prefer and I'll ask our Legal/Finance to update the SOW accordingly.

Thanks — excited to get this over the line.
— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
